channel.title: NewsCenter — All newsletter news — 2026-11-26
channel.description: Every news received through Laurent's newsletters over the last 24 hours. 110 news received.

item.title: FCC authorizes SpaceX’s one-million-unit AI satellite network
item.description: The FCC approved Starmind, SpaceX’s project to launch up to one million solar-powered satellites equipped with AI data centers. Despite opposition from Amazon, Viasat and astronomers, the first launches are scheduled for 2027 and the network must be completed by 2040.

item.title: OpenAI tests private inference for businesses
item.description: OpenAI’s Private Inference runs a company’s queries on its best models without OpenAI being able to see the data. The service is being tested with early business customers.

item.title: Epochal launches Time Portal, a “time machine” for AI
item.description: Startup Epochal, founded by former xAI members, unveiled Time Portal, an environment that confines AI agents to the Internet as it existed on a given date over the past 30-plus years. The agents then use this historical data to make forecasts, with sometimes surprisingly robust results.

item.title: SpaceX prepares to deploy computing capabilities in orbit
item.description: The U.S. space industry is generally described as being in poor health, while SpaceX is particularly well positioned to install computing infrastructure in orbit. The company has invested in this direction for more than a decade, while other technology giants lack ideas for future growth.

item.title: OpenAI claims to have demonstrated that the matrix multiplication exponent is 9/4
item.description: OpenAI claims to have proved that ω, the matrix multiplication exponent, is exactly equal to 9/4.

item.title: Anthropic’s IPO tests confidence in AI spending
item.description: Anthropic’s IPO provided a new test for bets on AI-related spending.

item.title: OpenAI, Google and Anthropic are designing their own chips
item.description: OpenAI, Google and Anthropic are using AI to design their own chips.

item.title: Elon Musk and SpaceX promise one share for every active Trump account
item.description: Elon Musk and SpaceX promise one share for every active Trump account.

item.title: OpenAI warns some heavy ChatGPT users about advanced limits
item.description: A small share of heavy ChatGPT users could reach limits more quickly when Chat and Work share the same usage counter. The rollout is expected to expand in December.

item.title: Meta reportedly negotiating with Amazon to let its Muse agent make purchases
item.description: Amazon and Meta are reportedly negotiating an agreement that would allow Meta’s Muse agent to make purchases on Amazon. The placement of ads and display of search results remain to be decided.

item.title: New York bans toys equipped with AI chatbots for five years
item.description: New York has become the second state, after California, to ban toys equipped with AI chatbots. The five-year ban will take effect 90 days after it is signed.

item.title: PrismML reduces a 27-billion-parameter coding model to 5.9 GB
item.description: Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B reduces a 27-billion-parameter programming model to 5.9 GB, about nine times smaller than usual. The open-source model can run on a Mac or an iPhone.

item.title: Carry saves and searches conversations from multiple AI assistants
item.description: Carry saves ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok conversations as Markdown files in a chosen folder, then lets users search them.

item.title: ChatGPT merges Chat and Work spaces with a shared quota
item.description: OpenAI is rolling out a single interface combining Chat and Work to some Pro subscribers, with a shared usage counter. A broader rollout is planned for December and could cause heavy users to hit their limits more quickly.

item.title: AI safety advocates turn away from Anthropic
item.description: According to The Information, some AI safety advocates are leaving Anthropic, believing that its rapid progress is increasing risks. They particularly criticize the company’s acceleration since its IPO.

item.title: My terrifying journey to becoming a real estate agent
item.description: It is far too easy to obtain a real estate agent’s license, which should worry American homebuyers. The author describes discovering the seedy side of every real estate sale.

item.title: Separate server and model costs to reduce an agent’s bill
item.description: Hosting a coding agent in the cloud generates two separate bills: infrastructure costs, charged for the entire runtime, and model costs, based on calls and tokens used. To avoid paying for idle time, shut down workspaces after tasks and track the two types of costs separately.

item.title: Nothing introduces Ear (note), earbuds that take notes with AI
item.description: Ear (note) records calls through the earbuds and in-person conversations through microphones built into the charging case. An app then turns the recordings into transcripts and quick summaries.

item.title: Grok Bot can call businesses and compile their responses
item.description: Grok Bot can be configured to call suppliers, restaurants, repair shops or service providers, ask a series of questions and compile the answers in a comparison. The user must approve each call, then can save the process as a skill and daily routine.

item.title: Grok Bot can monitor prices ahead of Black Friday
item.description: Grok Bot can monitor prices on Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy and other sites every few hours, then alert the user when the best deals appear.

item.title: Claude Fable 5.2 users are already exploring ambitious applications
item.description: Anthropic published an early look at real-world uses of Claude Fable 5.2 less than two weeks after its launch. Some examples go far beyond the most obvious use cases.

item.title: Independent developer creates a game with AI’s help in six days
item.description: A solo game developer says they used AI for the code and part of the visual work on their first game. Six days after launch, the title had surpassed a level of sales rarely achieved by independent developers.

item.title: Google files a patent to put you in personalized films and TV shows
item.description: Google has reportedly filed a patent for an AI-powered television network capable of using a person’s photos and voice to place them in personalized films and TV shows.

item.title: Rackspace shuts down Spot after security breach
item.description: Rackspace will permanently shut down its Spot Kubernetes service on December 8 at 5 p.m. Central Time. Customers must migrate their workloads and download their data, while API tokens, kubeconfigs and Kubernetes secrets are considered potentially compromised.

item.title: HPE shares fall amid declining AI-related margins
item.description: HPE shares fell about 16%, as its margin outlook overshadowed an improved 2027 revenue-growth forecast. Demand for AI servers is supporting revenue, but component costs are rising faster than selling prices.

item.title: European IT spending expected to jump 9.9% in 2027
item.description: Gartner forecasts that European IT spending will reach $1.57 trillion in 2027, up 9.9%. Demand for AI infrastructure and rising server prices are driving the increase, while software purchases are shifting toward systems that coordinate multiple business functions.

item.title: Why legacy systems are becoming increasingly risky
item.description: The reliability of aging infrastructure depends in part on maintenance, vendor support, replacement parts, monitoring and redundancy. Software becomes riskier as workloads evolve, patches disappear and support ends, making timely upgrades or retirement necessary.

item.title: An AI agent reveals a technical team’s unwritten rules
item.description: Matthew Finlayson describes creating an agent to route customer issues to engineering teams. The project uncovered undocumented ownership rules and improved routing accuracy from about 60% to 95%.

item.title: Claude supports skills, tasks and interactions through MCP
item.description: Anthropic is launching Skills over MCP in public beta for Claude, allowing Model Context Protocol servers to publish workflows and instructions alongside their tools. Tasks and Elicitation are also available for long-running and interactive work, while file uploads will be rolled out soon.

item.title: Datadog launches Bits Maintenance to automate infrastructure fixes
item.description: Datadog introduced Bits Maintenance, an AI teammate designed to automate patches and upgrades for open-source software. Available in preview, the tool tracks versions and vulnerabilities, analyzes changes, prepares upgrade plans and executes pull requests according to user-defined guardrails.

item.title: Workday’s CIO prepares IT for the AI era
item.description: Rani Johnson explains how Workday is rebuilding its data lake, identity infrastructure and Salesforce environment to strengthen its AI foundations. Collaboration with training helped increase enterprise AI adoption from under 50% to more than 96% by addressing skills and behavioral challenges.

item.title: Microsoft modernizes retail kiosks with Autopilot and Intune
item.description: Microsoft describes moving its point-of-sale devices from being domain-joined and managed by Configuration Manager to Windows Autopilot and Intune. The new setup uses Windows 11 Enterprise LTSC, Microsoft Entra join, provisioning without an individual user account and certificates for Wi-Fi access.

item.title: Capital One reduces human rework with its multi-agent system
item.description: Capital One reduced the rate of human rework on AI-generated customer-support summaries by about 80% with its MACAW agent system.

item.title: Germany’s federal IT provider chooses OpenProject as a Jira alternative
item.description: ITZBund, the central IT provider for Germany’s federal administration, chose OpenProject as an open-source alternative to Jira.

item.title: Google reorganizes Meet rooms’ “More actions” panel
item.description: Google Meet room-controller menus will prioritize the most frequently used commands. Early access rollout will begin on December 2, followed by broader rollout on December 11.

item.title: Neuralink receives FDA authorization to test its implant in ALS patients
item.description: The FDA authorized Neuralink to begin a trial of its LINK brain-computer interface with a limited number of ALS patients in the United States. The study will assess their ability to control digital devices with their thoughts, as well as the system’s long-term safety and reliability.

item.title: AI models outperform theoretical physicists on many technical tasks
item.description: Publicly accessible AI models crossed a threshold in August and now outperform most theoretical physicists on many technical tasks. They can perform complex analytical calculations, produce lengthy proofs and turn well-defined problems into code with little instruction.

item.title: Software engineering enters an advanced automation phase
item.description: A growing share of software work can be automated opaquely by teams, swarms or agent factories when the target is sufficiently verifiable. Advances in agents’ problem selection, intent and taste require continually redefining what needs human intervention.

item.title: Engineers who use AI can improve software quality
item.description: Equating engineers who use AI with executives who weaken their companies is harmful. With real responsibility and good models, engineers can build the safeguards, proofs and fixes they previously lacked time to create.

item.title: Anthropic operates like an infrastructure provider specializing in frontier AI
item.description: Anthropic is dedicating tens of billions of dollars in computing capacity to selling an advantage in AI and performance. The company is portrayed as a highly leveraged utility provider with an R&D department, able to preserve its margins through growing demand for frontier intelligence.

item.title: A guide to getting started in angel investing
item.description: Angel investing can potentially multiply a small investment many times over, and it is possible to start with $5,000. This article explains where beginners can find founders, how to evaluate them and how much to invest.

item.title: CSS mixins enable code blocks to be reused
item.description: A CSS mixin is a named block of code that developers can define once and reuse elsewhere in a stylesheet.

item.title: Ladybird’s first downloadable alpha shows promise
item.description: Ladybird’s rendering engine and LibJS JavaScript engine were written entirely from scratch. Its first downloadable alpha is surprisingly capable.

item.title: An introduction to open-source chip design
item.description: This article offers readers accustomed to a more software-oriented view of computing an introduction to the open-source chip-design toolchain.

item.title: The Jevons paradox may no longer explain rising usage
item.description: Cheaper tokens increase usage within the same stage, but moving to the next stage is an organizational rather than pricing problem.

item.title: Bicameral Labs seeks to create non-conscious neural networks
item.description: The founder of Bicameral Labs believes it is possible to create neural networks by ensuring that they are not conscious, or by minimizing the risk that they become conscious.

item.title: Cloud coding agents generate two separate costs to budget for
item.description: A cloud-hosted coding agent incurs separate infrastructure costs, tied to machine usage time, and model costs, tied to tokens consumed. To limit expenses, shut down workspaces when they are idle and track the two costs in separate columns.

item.title: A millennial popularizes Friendsgiving in a retirement community
item.description: A millennial introduced Friendsgiving to her neighbors in a retirement community, who first had to understand why the event took place on a different day. Four years later, it is the building’s most anticipated event.

item.title: AI may have contributed to the recent outages, but not as expected
item.description: AI likely played a role in the recent outages, but not in the way expected.

item.title: Cloudflare and Vercel call for calm amid AI fears
item.description: As social media imagined that AI could paralyze civilization, leaders at Cloudflare and Vercel called for calm.

item.title: JPMorgan supplier breach shows risks amplified by AI
item.description: A breach at a JPMorgan supplier illustrates why AI could make old vulnerabilities easier to exploit.

item.title: Black October PHP vulnerability illustrates AI risks
item.description: The Black October PHP vulnerability shows why AI could make exploiting old flaws easier.

item.title: Experts fear a “tsunami of vulnerabilities” with AI
item.description: Some experts believe AI could trigger a “tsunami of vulnerabilities.”

item.title: Jensen Huang’s return divides investors and tech leaders
item.description: Jensen Huang’s return divided investors and technology industry leaders.

item.title: AI is creating founders too important to fail
item.description: Jensen Huang’s return revived the question of whether AI is creating founders who have become too important to fail.

item.title: Jensen Huang says Nvidia does not need a Plan B
item.description: Jensen Huang said Nvidia did not need a Plan B.

item.title: S&P Global warns of dependence on Jensen Huang at Nvidia
item.description: S&P Global’s warning makes it harder to ignore the question of Jensen Huang’s succession at Nvidia.

item.title: Michael Burry criticizes Nvidia’s reliance on its leader
item.description: Michael Burry’s criticism adds to questions about Nvidia’s dependence on Jensen Huang.

item.title: Market decline raises questions about the profitability of AI spending
item.description: The market decline reflects growing doubts about whether companies investing heavily in data centers can generate sufficient returns.

item.title: Anthropic discloses nearly $895 billion in commitments
item.description: An amended document filed by Anthropic reports nearly $895 billion in commitments.

item.title: Anthropic shares fall below their IPO price
item.description: Anthropic shares fell below their IPO price less than a week after going public, signaling that investors still doubt revenues will exceed costs.

item.title: Google and Amazon could sell their chips to other customers
item.description: Google and Amazon could sell their chips to other customers.

item.title: Data center opposition could limit cloud capacity
item.description: Opposition to data centers could make it harder for major cloud providers to compete with existing capacity.

item.title: Macy’s Thanksgiving parade postponed until Saturday
item.description: A storm postponed Macy’s Thanksgiving parade until Saturday for the first time in its history, disrupting the plans of more than 3.5 million usual spectators.

item.title: Weather delays more than 6,500 U.S. flights
item.description: On Wednesday, weather delayed more than 6,500 flights in the United States and canceled about 160.

item.title: Nine things to know about the historic super El Niño
item.description: The article presents nine things to know about this year’s historic super El Niño.

item.title: Terence Tao calls for a transition to “math 2.0”
item.description: Terence Tao is calling for a transition to “math 2.0” following AI’s spectacular advances.

item.title: Anthropic gets more AI with less computing power
item.description: Anthropic is getting more AI with less computing power, which benefits the company but hurts other players.

item.title: Teen entrepreneur generates six-figure revenue in one month
item.description: A young entrepreneur ignored the advice to follow his passion. His business generated six-figure revenue in a single month.

item.title: The 10 best movies and shows to watch this weekend
item.description: The article recommends the 10 best movies and shows to watch during Thanksgiving weekend.

item.title: Bill Ackman shares Carl Icahn’s declining fortune
item.description: Bill Ackman cannot resist sharing information about Carl Icahn’s declining fortune.

item.title: Consumers are turning away from gift cards for more personal gifts
item.description: Gift cards are losing ground as consumers put more effort into their gifts this year.

item.title: Google is building a tollbooth for AI agents
item.description: Google is building a new tollbooth for AI agents, which could prompt Microsoft to do the same.

item.title: New notices exclude borrowers from a student repayment plan
item.description: Student loan borrowers are receiving new notices informing them that they have been excluded from an income-driven repayment plan.

item.title: Family who traveled to see the Thanksgiving parade will not be able to attend
item.description: Someone took their family to New York for the Thanksgiving parade, an event that had been on their dream list since childhood. They ultimately will not be able to see it.

item.title: Claude turns the United States into a Civilization map
item.description: Andrej Karpathy asked Claude Opus 5.5 to turn the United States into a Civilization map using public data. After seven hours and 45,000 lines of code, the map combines 31 sources on a hexagonal grid.

item.title: Anthropic’s CEO rejects the idea of an AI-governed society
item.description: Dario Amodei believes humans should not hand society’s major decisions over to AI. He advocates governing AI through legitimate democratic processes, while distinguishing task execution from writing collective rules.

item.title: A coding agent must demonstrate every performance gain
item.description: The Agentic Algorithm Engineering project requires Claude Code and Codex to define a benchmark, a metric, correctness checks and a budget before any optimization. In examples involving KaHIP and VieCut, the agent kept only changes that were faster and correct.

item.title: Perplexity launches a spoiler-free Internet
item.description: Perplexity has created a spoiler-free Internet to test whether an AI can predict an election without Google revealing the result to it.

item.title: Democratic senators call for new AI restrictions
item.description: Several Democratic senators have called for new AI restrictions following reports that laboratory employees fear some internal models are too dangerous to release.

item.title: Agents already control some of the computing used by Gemini
item.description: Koray Kavukcuoglu, a vice president at Google DeepMind, said that AI agents now control some of the computing used in Gemini experiments, while estimating that full self-improvement remains a long way off.

item.title: Claude can now acquire skills through MCP servers
item.description: Skills over MCP gives Claude instructions for using a connected application without a separate installation. The feature is in public beta and enabled by default for Pro, Max and Ultra subscriptions.

item.title: Cloudflare adds search for AI agents
item.description: Cloudflare’s Search for Agents adds a search endpoint to a website that AI agents can query and that returns Markdown. The feature has been available in beta from the dashboard.

item.title: CodeRabbit Verify tests applications and posts errors on PRs
item.description: CodeRabbit Verify runs an application in a sandbox on demand, then posts encountered issues to the pull request along with recordings, screenshots and logs. The service is in public beta.

item.title: MemoryWorks centralizes engineering decisions and team knowledge
item.description: MemoryWorks brings an engineering team’s decisions and knowledge together in a searchable knowledge base for employees and AI agents, with links to the sources.

item.title: Claude writes 80% of Anthropic’s code, but Amodei wants to limit its autonomy
item.description: According to Anthropic, Claude wrote more than 80% of the code merged into its codebase in June 2026. Dario Amodei wants to set a limit on recursive self-improvement and refuses to let AI build future models alone without human oversight.

item.title: Google imagines a personalized AI TV channel where you would play the lead role
item.description: A patent describes “My Channel,” a service that continuously produces AI-generated videos from personal data, with the option to appear as the protagonist. The system would also incorporate personalized ads.

item.title: The Hera probe reveals a stadium-sized crater on Dimorphos
item.description: The European Hera probe photographed the damage from DART’s deliberate impact on the asteroid Dimorphos. The crater spans its entire width, and hundreds of rocks now orbit the asteroid.

item.title: Google DeepMind entrusts Gemini experiments to AI agents
item.description: AI agents independently launch and run some of the experiments preparing future Gemini models. DeepMind leaves their internal reasoning untrained so humans can review it.

item.title: MIT improves climate forecasts using extreme scenarios
item.description: By training its models on deliberately abrupt changes in CO2 and methane, an MIT team has produced more robust climate emulators. A single training run is now sufficient instead of six to eight.

item.title: Researchers define five trust conditions for AI agents
item.description: Ai2 surveyed 17 scientists about using AI agents in their work. They identified five conditions for trust: validation, privacy, objectivity, accountability and transparency.

item.title: Embo-Harness lets AI models directly control robots
item.description: This framework allows multimodal models to plan actions and use tools to control robots from a simple instruction. It achieves an 83.3% success rate on RoboLab-120 and succeeds in 15 of 20 trials on real robots.

item.title: Vibe coding pushes synthesizer makers toward open source
item.description: Hobbyists are modifying electronic instrument firmware with agents such as Claude and the Reverse Engineer Anything tool. InMusic, the parent company of Akai, Moog and Native Instruments, has chosen to open-source its devices’ code.

item.title: NVIDIA releases training data for Nemotron 3.5 Parse
item.description: NVIDIA has open-sourced the training data for Nemotron 3.5 Parse, including 9.98 million charts, one million tables and 7.9 million multilingual pages. The model converts page images into structured data.

item.title: Chinese labs estimate they are up to nine months behind the United States
item.description: Chip restrictions, limited access to Nvidia hardware and anti-distillation measures are weighing on DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and Alibaba. DeepSeek researchers reportedly estimate internally that they are no more than nine months behind.

item.title: 42 attorneys general seek to stop Character.AI from selling conversations
item.description: In bankruptcy, Character.AI plans to sell its assets, including users’ chat histories and IP addresses, many of them belonging to minors. Forty-two attorneys general are asking the court to block the sale.

item.title: Nvidia risks a ratings downgrade amid political controversy
item.description: S&P placed Nvidia on negative watch following controversy involving Jensen Huang and an alleged investigation by the Department of Justice. The agency could downgrade the company from AA to AA- within 90 days.

item.title: CIA and U.S. intelligence agencies hit by intrusion
item.description: The CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence discovered an intrusion into a public-intelligence analysis system. The data was not classified, but the extent of the leak remains unknown.

item.title: SoftBank rebounds after a 14.8% stock-market plunge
item.description: After falling 14.8% in a single session, SoftBank rebounded more than 11% on Thursday. Asian chip stocks also rose after doubts about the profitability of AI spending.

item.title: Access to new medicines in Switzerland: an emerging risk?
item.description: The editorial questions whether people in Switzerland may soon lose access to new medicines, despite having the ability to develop or produce them.

item.title: Parkinson’s: sleep brain waves linked to hallucinations
item.description: A study seeks to explain why some people with Parkinson’s experience hallucinations or cognitive difficulties by linking these symptoms to sleep-related brain waves.

item.title: Nuclear fusion: EPFL solves a more-than-40-year-old mystery
item.description: Since 1982, physicists have known that plasma heated beyond a certain threshold can suddenly change its behavior. EPFL has provided an answer to this mystery involving nuclear fusion plasma.

item.title: Proteins from ancient viruses control our genes
item.description: A significant portion of the human genome comes from ancient mobile genetic elements, some of which originated from ancient viruses. These proteins now control the activity of our genes.

item.title: Cryptography: the quantum threat could become critical as early as 2030
item.description: Quantum computers cannot yet break major encryption systems. However, the threat could become critical as early as 2030.

item.title: Riemann Hypothesis: an AI and a mathematician propose two proofs
item.description: One of mathematics’ greatest open problems may have reached a historic milestone. An AI and a mathematician claim to have produced two competing proofs.

item.title: In Basel, AI reveals how the DNA environment activates genes
item.description: Nearly all cells possess the same DNA, but they do not activate the same genes. Researchers in Basel are using AI to study the role of the DNA environment.

item.title: DNA repair: how the cell chooses its strategy
item.description: When both strands of a chromosome break, the cell must act quickly to prevent damage. Swiss researchers reveal how it chooses its repair strategy.

item.title: Tuberculosis: a shared membrane strengthens bacterial resistance
item.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis can form long, membrane-like structures. This shared membrane helps the bacteria resist the body’s defenses.

item.title: Primordial plasma challenges an Einstein diffusion model
item.description: More than 120 years after Albert Einstein’s work on Brownian motion, a study challenges a diffusion model applied to primordial plasma.

item.title: How Copilot turns financial PDFs into a dashboard
item.description: Copilot gathered financial documents in OneLake, then Fabric extracted the data from the PDFs, created a semantic model, and generated an application. Satya Nadella received a link to the dashboard about 30 to 35 minutes later.
